text:
Ravi P: Heads up 1: we need to finalize the transport story for internal model routing. Two options on the table: proto-first gRPC internal with thin JSON facade, or plain JSON everywhere. Need to consider quotas, routing labels for the console, and rollout UX.

Jules: Proto-first almost always for performance. We can attach metadata in gRPC headers for model_variant, batch_size, and quota_key. Saves us from parsing request bodies in edge proxies.

Marta (PM): Console requirement: stable, human-readable route identifiers that persist across refactors and rollouts. Also want a toggle to show canary vs baseline traffic for each route.

Theo: If we go gRPC, we need a canonical identifier surface that all infra uses. Suggestion: the edge gateway injects X-Rdwd-Route which normalizes to product-level names like inference.chat.completions.v1. That header becomes the single source of truth for dashboards and quota checks.

Ravi P: Who owns mapping logic? Gateway rulebook or service code? If gateway owns it, we can avoid changing services during refactors. If services own it, they'll be closer to actual operation semantics.

Jules: Gateway-owned mapping is easier operationally. Add a verification step in CI so services validate the canonical label they expect is present. That prevents silent drift.

Marta (PM): Also important: tenants want per-route soft-limits and hard-limits. Soft-limits emit warnings in console; hard-limits reject. Quota key must include tenant id and canonical route.

Theo: Proposal for quota key format: tenant_id|canonical_route|window. We can hash it for storage but keep readable labels in telemetry.

Ravi P: Security concern: clients could set X-Rdwd-Route. Gateway must strip incoming header and set its own value after authn/authz. Also record the original :path or method in raw logs for debug.

Jules: Implementation note: Envoy Lua/filter to translate path -> canonical and then overwrite header. Example pseudo:

```lua
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local path = request_handle:headers():get(":path")
  local canonical = route_map[path] or path
  request_handle:headers():replace("x-rdwd-route", canonical)
end
```

Marta (PM): Nice. For the console, can we emit both canonical and legacy labels during a migration window so dashboards show both? That would help product teams reconcile metrics.

Theo: Yep. Telemetry producers should write tags: canonical_route, legacy_route, service_name. Aggregation pipeline can roll them up. We'll need a migration flag in the console to toggle showing legacy names.

Ravi P: Rollout UX: when we spin a canary model, we want to route X% of traffic from a canonical route to the canary variant without changing the canonical label. The console should show variant-level breakdown under the same canonical route.

Jules: So canonical is orthogonal to model variant. Telemetry keys: canonical|variant|tenant. Good. Token accounting works per tenant+canonical, variant breakdown only for diagnostics.

Marta (PM): Also request sampling for traces: sample 1% by default, 100% on error. Add a flag so we can increase sampling for canary cohorts.

Theo: We'll wire sampling controls into the rollout config. Envoy can add a sampling header that tracing collector understands.

eng-deploy-bot: Canary: transport-proxy-spike v0.3 -> canary group (3/4 hosts) :white_check_mark: metrics stream connected

Ravi P: Action items: Jules to prototype Envoy header transform + mapping rules. Theo to extend telemetry schema to include canonical_route and legacy_route tags. Marta will draft console migration UX and canary breakdown. I'll own quota key design + phi for storage.

Marta (PM): Timeline: 5-day spike. Demo end of next week with a small browser -> gateway -> gRPC service flow showing p95, token-cost, and variant split.

Jules: One more note: for non-HTTP transports (e.g., unix sockets inside k8s), ensure the canonical header is propagated as metadata. We'll need a small middleware to translate header <-> metadata.

Theo: I'll add a small middleware in the tracing/propagation lib to keep parity.

Ravi P: Sounds good. Let's keep the spike focused: mapping rules, header enforcement, quota key format, and a very small console mock showing canonical vs legacy.

Marta (PM): Added ticket https://go/infra/178123-proto-facade-migration (placeholder).

Ravi P: Thanks team.
